name: Jupiter Power
headquarters: Austin, Texas, United States (offices: Houston, Chicago)
ownership: private — owned by funds managed by BlackRock's Diversified Infrastructure business (acquired from EnCap Investments/Yorktown/Mercuria, announced Nov 2022, value undisclosed); current site describes Jupiter as 'backed by Global Infrastructure Partners (GIP), part of BlackRock'
summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: Jupiter Power is Hithium's most important disclosed US customer — a BlackRock-owned standalone-storage IPP with ~8,800 MWh operating/under-construction/contracted, a 20 GW / 97 GWh development pipeline across 8 RTOs, and a verified three-layer Hithium relationship: the June 20, 2024 supply agreement for 3 GWh of ∞Block 5 MWh containers (314 Ah cells, delivery by end-2025 — timing that landed the equipment inside the pre-2026 FEOC safe-harbor window); Jupiter's naming in Hithium's HKEX prospectus partner roster (per ess-news coverage); and a confirmed design win at Trimount, Everett MA — the largest planned BESS in New England at 700 MW/2,800 MWh, specified with Hithium 5.015 MWh units (Energy-Storage.News, Mar 2026). The asymmetry matters: Jupiter's own channels have never once mentioned Hithium, while publicly messaging domestic content — an Energy Vault 2.4 GWh domestic-content LOI (2022), a Peak Energy sodium-ion agreement up to 4.75 GWh (Nov 2025), and a $500M credit facility earmarked partly for 'domestic battery storage procurement' (Jan 2026).
ecosystemRole: We assess Jupiter as the reference account in the Hithium-US story and the single best window into how a top-tier US buyer actually manages a Chinese supplier relationship post-FEOC: buy big and quietly inside the safe-harbor window, never co-market, and hedge loudly with domestic supply. Jupiter is also a first-mover franchise collector — first tolled battery in ERCOT (Crossett), Houston's first large BESS (Callisto), Michigan's first utility-scale BESS (Tibbits), and New England's largest planned battery (Trimount) — with an in-house trading desk Modo Energy repeatedly benchmarks among ERCOT's best (its Swoose asset was ERCOT's top-earning battery in Nov 2024). Its AIDC posture is siting-led rather than contract-led: urban load-pocket brownfields (Callisto in Houston, Trimount at Boston's Mystic node) positioned as fast firm capacity for AI-era load, with no named data-center offtake yet — the undisclosed Tidwell Prairie Phase I toll counterparty is the one place a hyperscaler could be hiding.

productsAndServices.name: ERCOT operating fleet (the merchant cash engine)
productsAndServices.description: Texas fleet built from 2021: Flower Valley I (9.9 MW/19.8 MWh) and II (100 MW/200 MWh, Reeves Co.), Crossett (200 MW/200 MWh, Crane Co.), Swoose I (9.9 MW) and II (100 MW/200 MWh, Ward Co.), St Gall (100 MW/200 MWh, Fort Stockton — Energy Vault build on Rept modules, COD Jul 2024), Callisto I (200 MW/400 MWh, central Houston brownfield on the former HL&P H.O. Clarke plant site, COD Aug 2024, expandable +400 MW/800 MWh), Tidwell Prairie phases (Robertson Co. — Phase I 200 MW long-term toll with undisclosed offtaker, delayed past summer 2025; Phase IIA 100 MW/200 MWh under a 10-yr Denton Municipal Electric PPA, COD Jun 2026; Phase III targeted 2027, interconnection unsecured as of Oct 2025).
productsAndServices.positioning: One of the largest ERCOT storage owners (grouped by Modo with Enel, SMT and Tesla among 2025's biggest adders; reported third owner past 1 GWh installed alongside Plus Power and ENGIE — aggregator-level). Mostly 1-2 hour duration — shorter than Eolian's 4-5-hour push.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Merchant-plus-selective-contracting: in-house 24/7 trading desk with proprietary AI/ML dispatch optimization; tolls and PPAs layered on (Crossett I toll with Hatch EQ I/Equilibrium — the first known tolled battery in ERCOT; Austin Energy up-to-$288M/100 MW 20-yr deal, Oct 2025).
productsAndServices.targetSegments: ERCOT energy/ancillary markets, municipal utilities (Denton, Austin Energy), corporate tolls.
productsAndServices.roadmap: Callisto expansion option; Tidwell Prairie Phase III; ERCOT revenue compression (2025 fleet revenues roughly one-sixth of 2023 per Modo) pushes the mix toward contracted structures.

productsAndServices.name: National expansion fleet (MISO, ISO-NE, PJM, WECC)
productsAndServices.description: Tibbits (100 MW/400 MWh, Coldwater MI — Michigan's first operational utility-scale BESS, COD summer 2025, 20-yr Consumers Energy PPA) and Voyager (100 MW, Saline Twp MI, second Consumers PPA) in MISO; Trimount (700 MW/2,800 MWh, Everett MA — former ExxonMobil terminal at the Eversource Mystic substation, final EFSB approval Feb 27, 2026, ~$500M-$1B investment, target 2027, Hithium 5.015 MWh units) and Streamfield (200 MW, Westfield MA, construction 2026) in ISO-NE; Woods Landing (~200-275 MW, Sayreville NJ, retired coal site) and Prairie Flyer (85 MW, Vandalia OH) in PJM; Liberty I & II (380 MW combined, Madison Co. IN, I&M purchase agreement pending IURC); Blackberry Grove (100 MW, OR) and Cascadia Ridge (130 MW, WA) in the Northwest. Oyster Shore (Long Island, ~275 MW) was terminated — 'no viable permit path.'
productsAndServices.positioning: The East Coast beachhead most ERCOT-native peers lack — Trimount is the largest battery ever to clear a PJM-style capacity commitment in its market class... its ISO-NE positioning at metro Boston's constrained Mystic node is the marquee siting play.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Long-term utility PPAs (Consumers 20-yr, I&M) plus merchant/capacity in ISO-NE; balance-sheet and project-financed construction.
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Capacity-constrained load centers; utilities retiring coal/gas with interconnection positions to reuse.
productsAndServices.roadmap: Trimount COD 2027 (the flagship Hithium delivery to watch); Liberty I construction 2027/COD 2028; 20,000+ MW development pipeline across 8 RTOs (company-claimed, with internal inconsistencies — a 12 GW figure persisted in Jan 2026 PR).

productsAndServices.name: Procurement & supply program
productsAndServices.description: Three public strands: (1) Energy Vault — 2022 agreements totaling 220 MWh (St Gall + Carpinteria CA) plus a Sep 2022 LOI for 2.4 GWh of domestic-content-qualified BESS targeting the IRA domestic-content bonus; Energy Vault delivered St Gall with B-VAULT AC blocks on Rept Battero modules and won further orders (a 400 MWh project in early 2024; a second 100 MW/200 MWh ERCOT project, Jun 2025). (2) Hithium — 3 GWh of ∞Block 5 MWh DC blocks (Jun 2024, delivery by end-2025), CTO Michael Geier quoted; plus the Trimount design win. (3) Peak Energy — up to 4.75 GWh of US-made sodium-ion (Nov 2025; ~720 MWh delivery 2027, the largest sodium-ion deployment announced to date, contract value potentially >$500M).
productsAndServices.positioning: A barbell strategy: safe-harbored Chinese supply for near-term GWh, domestic-content options (Energy Vault, Peak sodium-ion) for bonus credits and post-2026 FEOC compliance. Which projects absorbed the 3 GWh is never itemized — candidates by timing are Tidwell Prairie, Tibbits, and pre-delivered Trimount equipment (inference).
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct OEM supply agreements + integrator/EPC relationships (Energy Vault); no cell chemistry or vendor named on Jupiter's own site for any project.
productsAndServices.roadmap: Jan 2026 $500M facility proceeds earmarked partly for 'domestic battery storage procurement' — the forward book tilts domestic unless FEOC-compliant structures reopen the Chinese lane.

productsAndServices.name: Trading & optimization platform
productsAndServices.description: In-house 24/7 trading desk (led by CRO Laura Wellborn, trading since the first assets came online in 2021), proprietary dispatch/optimization software with AI/ML price forecasting — 'unparalleled intellectual property in dispatch optimization' (company language). Modo Energy repeatedly uses Jupiter as a named optimizer case study; Swoose was ERCOT's highest-earning battery in Nov 2024 at more than 2× the BESS index (non-spin-heavy strategy).
productsAndServices.positioning: Optimization pedigree is the durable differentiator as ERCOT spreads compress — and the reason Jupiter can carry merchant exposure peers contract away.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Internal fleet dispatch; contracted structures (tolls) sell dispatch rights while keeping operations in-house.
productsAndServices.roadmap: ERCOT RTC+B market redesign (2026) changes dispatch economics — Modo benchmarks continue to track Jupiter through the transition.

strategyRead: (High confidence) We assess Jupiter as Hithium's single most valuable US relationship and reference: a verified 3 GWh supply agreement, a prospectus-level customer naming, and the Trimount 2.8 GWh design win — likely the largest disclosed Hithium commitment by any US buyer. Servicing Trimount flawlessly through its 2027 COD is the highest-leverage account-management task in Hithium's US book.

(High confidence) We assess the relationship as deliberately unreciprocated in public: Jupiter has never named Hithium in its own channels while actively messaging domestic content (Energy Vault domestic LOI, Peak sodium-ion, 'domestic battery storage procurement' financing language). Expect continued quiet-buyer behavior — no co-marketing, no logo rights — and calibrate reference-selling accordingly.

(Moderate confidence) We assess Jupiter's post-2025 procurement as tilting domestic by default: the safe-harbor window that enabled the 3 GWh closed Dec 31, 2025; the pipeline's ITC economics now demand FEOC-compliant supply; and the Peak/Energy Vault strands exist precisely to cover that. A follow-on Chinese-content order requires either safe-harbored inventory (opaque) or a compliant structure Hithium does not yet publicly have.

(Moderate confidence) We assess the AIDC angle as siting-led and latent: no named data-center offtake exists, but Callisto (Houston), Trimount (Boston/Mystic), and the CEO's public framing of storage as the fast answer to data-center-driven load position the fleet for large-load contracting — and the undisclosed Tidwell Prairie Phase I toll counterparty is worth intelligence effort.

(High confidence) For the Hithium lens: protect and expand this account through delivery excellence (Trimount), Mesquite-based US assembly where it helps optics, and patience on co-marketing — while recognizing that Jupiter's leadership reshuffle (Nov 2025) and BlackRock/GIP sponsor-level procurement norms (shared with sibling Eolian, a vocal American-built advocate) could tighten the door over time.

relationships.note: 3 GWh ∞Block supply agreement + the Trimount 2.8 GWh design win — Hithium's most important disclosed US customer relationship.
relationships.context:
Three verified layers: the June 20, 2024 supply agreement for 3 GWh of ∞Block 5 MWh containers (314 Ah cells, delivery by end-2025 — timing that landed the equipment inside the pre-2026 FEOC safe-harbor window, CTO Michael Geier quoted); Jupiter's naming in Hithium's HKEX prospectus partner roster; and the confirmed design win at Trimount, Everett MA — the largest planned BESS in New England (700 MW/2,800 MWh, Hithium 5.015 MWh units, final EFSB approval Feb 27, 2026, target 2027).

The asymmetry is deliberate: Jupiter's own channels have never mentioned Hithium while publicly messaging domestic content (Energy Vault domestic-content LOI, Peak Energy sodium-ion agreement up to 4.75 GWh, financing language earmarking 'domestic battery storage procurement') — the template for how a top-tier US buyer manages a Chinese supplier post-FEOC: buy big quietly inside the safe-harbor window, never co-market, hedge loudly.

relationships.note: Sponsor sibling under BlackRock since the GIP absorption.
relationships.context: BlackRock (Diversified Infrastructure) bought Jupiter in 2022; the 2024 GIP absorption made Jupiter and Eolian sponsor siblings. If sponsor-level procurement norms harmonize, the dossier assesses they harmonize toward Eolian's vocal American-built doctrine — the quiet long-term risk to Jupiter's pragmatic Chinese-supply posture.
